name: Management
description: The practice and study of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling organizations and their resources.

name: Organizational Behavior
description: The study of how individuals and groups behave within organizations.

name: Human Resource Management
description: The management of people, employment relationships, and the workforce of an organization.

name: Operations Management
description: The design and control of the processes that produce goods and deliver services.

name: Supply Chain Management
description: The coordination of the flow of materials, information, and funds across organizations from suppliers to customers.

name: Marketing
description: The study of creating, communicating, and delivering value to customers and markets.

name: Strategic Management
description: The formulation and execution of long-term goals and competitive positioning of organizations.

name: Entrepreneurship
description: The study of identifying opportunities and creating, financing, and growing new ventures.

name: International Business
description: The study of business activities that cross national borders and operate in multiple country contexts.

name: Management Information Systems
description: The study of how information technology supports, transforms, and enables organizations and their processes.

name: Business Ethics
description: The study of moral principles and standards as they apply to business conduct and decisions.

name: Corporate Governance
description: The system of rules and practices by which companies are directed, controlled, and held accountable.

name: Business Analytics
description: The use of data, statistics, and modeling to support evidence-based business decisions.

name: Project Management
description: The discipline of planning, executing, and closing temporary endeavors with defined scope, time, and cost.

name: Innovation Management
description: The management of processes, structures, and culture that generate and commercialize novel ideas.

name: Organization Theory
description: The study of organizations as entities: their design, structure, environments, and change.

name: Management Theory
description: The historical and contemporary schools of thought about how management should be practiced.

name: Scientific Management
description: The early twentieth-century school applying time-and-motion study to optimize worker efficiency.

name: Administrative Management
description: Fayol's school defining the universal functions and principles of administration.

name: Bureaucratic Management
description: Weber's model of rational-legal authority based on hierarchy, rules, and impersonal roles.

name: Human Relations School
description: The school emphasizing social needs and informal groups in worker productivity, rooted in the Hawthorne studies.

name: Contingency Theory
description: The view that there is no single best way to manage and that optimal structure depends on context.

name: Systems Approach to Management
description: The school viewing organizations as open systems of interdependent parts interacting with their environment.

name: Planning
description: The managerial function of setting objectives and determining the means to achieve them.

name: Leadership
description: The study of influencing and motivating people toward shared goals.

name: Transformational Leadership
description: Leadership that inspires followers through vision, idealized influence, and intellectual stimulation.

name: Servant Leadership
description: Leadership that prioritizes serving followers' needs and development ahead of the leader's own interests.

name: Situational Leadership
description: Leadership that adapts style to the readiness and competence of followers.

name: Managerial Decision Making
description: The study of how managers identify problems, evaluate alternatives, and choose courses of action.

name: Change Management
description: The structured approach to transitioning organizations, teams, and individuals through change.

name: Performance Management
description: The continuous process of aligning, measuring, and improving individual and organizational performance.

name: Knowledge Management
description: The capture, organization, sharing, and use of organizational knowledge and expertise.

name: Quality Management
description: The discipline of ensuring products and processes meet quality standards and continuously improve.

name: Total Quality Management
description: An organization-wide, customer-focused approach to continuous quality improvement.

name: Six Sigma
description: A data-driven methodology for reducing defects and process variation to near-perfect levels.

name: Lean Management
description: A methodology for maximizing customer value while minimizing waste, rooted in the Toyota Production System.

name: Nonprofit Management
description: The management of mission-driven organizations that reinvest surplus rather than distributing profit.

name: Crisis Management
description: The preparation for, response to, and recovery from events that threaten an organization's viability.

name: Sustainability Management
description: The integration of environmental and social performance into corporate strategy and operations.

name: Motivation
description: The study of the psychological forces that energize, direct, and sustain work effort.

name: Personality and Values
description: The study of individual differences in personality traits and values and their effect on behavior at work.

name: Work Attitudes
description: The study of job satisfaction, organizational commitment, and employee engagement.

name: Group Dynamics
description: The study of how groups form, function, and influence their members.

name: Teams and Team Effectiveness
description: The study of work teams, their composition, processes, and performance.

name: Group Decision Making
description: The study of how decisions are made collectively, including groupthink and participation.

name: Organizational Communication
description: The study of how information and meaning flow within and between organizations.

name: Power and Politics
description: The study of influence, authority, and political behavior in organizations.

name: Negotiation
description: The study of bargaining and conflict resolution between parties with interdependent interests.

name: Organizational Culture
description: The study of the shared values, beliefs, and norms that shape how organizational members act.

name: Organization Development
description: The planned, systematic use of behavioral science to improve organizational effectiveness and health.

name: Work Stress and Well-being
description: The study of occupational stress, burnout, and employee well-being.

name: Workplace Diversity and Inclusion
description: The study of workforce diversity and practices that foster inclusion and equity.

name: Organizational Justice
description: The study of employees' perceptions of fairness in distributions, procedures, and treatment.

name: Job Analysis and Design
description: The systematic study and structuring of jobs, tasks, and responsibilities.

name: Workforce Planning
description: Forecasting and planning the staffing needs of an organization over time.

name: Recruitment and Selection
description: Attracting, assessing, and hiring qualified candidates for open positions.

name: Training and Development
description: Designing and delivering learning experiences that build employee skills and careers.

name: Performance Appraisal
description: The formal evaluation and feedback of employee performance against standards.

name: Compensation and Benefits
description: The design of pay structures, incentives, and employee benefit programs.

name: Employee and Labor Relations
description: Managing the relationship between employers, employees, and unions, including collective bargaining.

name: Talent Management
description: The integrated attraction, development, retention, and succession of key talent.

name: Strategic Human Resource Management
description: Aligning HR systems and practices with organizational strategy and goals.

name: International Human Resource Management
description: Managing people across borders, including expatriation and global staffing.

name: People Analytics
description: The use of data and statistics to inform workforce decisions.

name: Process Analysis and Design
description: Mapping, measuring, and redesigning the activities that transform inputs into outputs.

name: Capacity Management
description: Planning and controlling the maximum output an operation can produce.

name: Inventory Management
description: Controlling the quantity, location, and timing of stocked materials and finished goods.

name: Scheduling
description: Assigning work, resources, and time slots to tasks and jobs.

name: Demand Forecasting
description: Predicting future customer demand to plan production and resources.

name: Facility Location and Layout
description: Deciding where facilities should be located and how their physical space should be arranged.

name: Service Operations Management
description: The design and delivery of intangible services, including capacity and queue management.

name: Lean Operations
description: Applying lean principles to eliminate waste and improve flow in operations.

name: Theory of Constraints
description: A management philosophy focusing on identifying and managing the bottleneck that limits throughput.

name: Operations Strategy
description: Aligning operational capabilities and decisions with competitive strategy.

name: Procurement and Sourcing
description: Acquiring goods and services, and selecting and managing suppliers.

name: Logistics
description: The management of the physical flow and storage of goods through the supply chain.

name: Transportation Management
description: Planning and optimizing the movement of goods by road, rail, sea, and air.

name: Warehousing
description: The design and operation of facilities that store goods between supply chain stages.

name: Distribution Management
description: Managing the channels and networks that deliver products to customers.

name: Reverse Logistics
description: Managing the return, reuse, recycling, and disposal of products.

name: Demand Planning
description: Forecasting and shaping customer demand to align supply with market needs.

name: Sales and Operations Planning
description: The integrated cross-functional process balancing demand, supply, and financial plans.

name: Supplier Relationship Management
description: Systematically managing interactions and collaboration with suppliers.

name: Supply Chain Risk Management
description: Identifying and mitigating disruptions and vulnerabilities in supply networks.

name: Sustainable Supply Chain Management
description: Managing supply chains to reduce environmental and social impacts.

name: Consumer Behavior
description: The study of how individuals and groups select, buy, use, and dispose of goods and services.

name: Marketing Research
description: The systematic collection and analysis of data about markets and customers.

name: Marketing Strategy
description: Choosing target markets and designing the value proposition and mix to serve them.

name: Market Segmentation
description: Dividing a market into distinct groups of buyers with similar needs or behaviors.

name: Targeting and Positioning
description: Selecting segments to serve and crafting a distinct place in buyers' minds.

name: Brand Management
description: Building and managing a brand's identity, meaning, and equity over time.

name: Brand Equity
description: The value a brand adds to a product through awareness, associations, and loyalty.

name: Pricing Strategy
description: Setting prices to capture value, considering cost, competition, and demand.

name: Product Management
description: Managing a product's lifecycle, features, and positioning in the market.

name: Channel Management
description: Designing and managing the distribution channels through which products reach buyers.

name: Advertising
description: Paid, mediated communication intended to inform or persuade an audience about offerings.

name: Sales Promotion
description: Short-term incentives designed to stimulate immediate purchase.

name: Public Relations
description: Managing communication and relationships between an organization and its publics.

name: Digital Marketing
description: Marketing through digital channels and technologies, including the internet and mobile devices.

name: Search Engine Marketing
description: Using paid and organic search visibility to drive traffic and conversions.

name: Social Media Marketing
description: Using social platforms to build audiences, engage customers, and promote offerings.

name: Content Marketing
description: Creating and distributing valuable content to attract and retain a defined audience.

name: Influencer Marketing
description: Partnering with influential individuals to promote products to their audiences.

name: Integrated Marketing Communications
description: Coordinating all promotional tools and messages into a unified, consistent whole.

name: Services Marketing
description: Marketing intangible offerings, emphasizing quality, relationships, and customer experience.

name: Business-to-Business Marketing
description: Marketing goods and services to organizational rather than individual buyers.

name: International Marketing
description: Adapting and coordinating marketing strategy across multiple countries and cultures.

name: Relationship Marketing
description: Building long-term, mutually beneficial relationships with customers rather than one-off transactions.

name: Retail Management
description: Managing the merchandising, operations, and experience of retail businesses.

name: Marketing Analytics
description: Measuring, modeling, and optimizing marketing performance with data.

name: Strategic Analysis
description: Diagnosing the external and internal environment to inform strategic choices.

name: Industry Analysis
description: Assessing the structure and attractiveness of an industry, as in Porter's Five Forces.

name: Competitive Analysis
description: Evaluating rivals' strategies, resources, and likely moves.

name: Resource-Based View
description: The theory that sustained advantage arises from valuable, rare, inimitable resources and capabilities.

name: Business-Level Strategy
description: How a firm competes within a particular market through cost leadership, differentiation, or focus.

name: Corporate-Level Strategy
description: Decisions about what businesses a corporation should be in and how to manage them.

name: Diversification
description: Entering new products or markets, related or unrelated to the current business.

name: Mergers and Acquisitions
description: Combining or acquiring firms to achieve strategic and financial objectives.

name: Vertical Integration
description: Expanding into upstream suppliers or downstream distribution stages of the value chain.

name: Global Strategy
description: How firms coordinate strategy across international markets and location choices.

name: Business Model
description: The logic by which an organization creates, delivers, and captures value.

name: Strategy Implementation
description: Translating strategy into action through structure, systems, and culture.

name: Scenario Planning
description: Developing and reasoning about multiple plausible futures to guide strategy under uncertainty.

name: Platform Strategy
description: Strategy for multi-sided platforms that create value by facilitating interactions between groups.

name: Opportunity Recognition
description: Identifying and evaluating unmet needs and possibilities for new value creation.

name: Business Planning
description: Developing the plan that describes a venture's model, market, and financial projections.

name: Lean Startup
description: A methodology of iterative experimentation, minimum viable products, and validated learning.

name: Startup Financing
description: The sources and structures of funding for new and growing ventures.

name: Venture Capital
description: Equity financing from funds that invest in high-growth, high-risk startups.

name: Angel Investing
description: Early-stage equity funding from affluent individuals, often before institutional capital.

name: Crowdfunding
description: Raising small amounts of capital from a large number of people, usually online.

name: Bootstrapping
description: Building a venture using internal cash flow and personal resources rather than outside funding.

name: Social Entrepreneurship
description: Creating ventures that pursue social or environmental impact through market-based means.

name: Corporate Entrepreneurship
description: Entrepreneurial activity within established firms.

name: Small Business Management
description: The management of independently owned small firms and their distinctive challenges.

name: Family Business
description: The study of businesses owned and managed across family generations, including succession.

name: Technology Entrepreneurship
description: Creating ventures that commercialize technological innovation.

name: Foreign Market Entry
description: The modes and strategies for entering foreign markets, from exporting to wholly owned subsidiaries.

name: Multinational Enterprise Management
description: Managing firms that operate production and sales across multiple countries.

name: Cross-Cultural Management
description: Managing and working across national cultures, as in Hofstede's dimensions.

name: Export and Import Management
description: Managing cross-border trade transactions, documentation, and compliance.

name: Emerging Markets
description: The study of business opportunities and institutions in developing and transitional economies.

name: Offshoring and Outsourcing
description: Relocating business activities abroad or contracting them to external providers.

name: IT Governance
description: The framework for aligning IT with business goals and ensuring accountability for IT decisions.

name: Enterprise Systems
description: Integrated, organization-wide information systems supporting core business processes.

name: Enterprise Resource Planning
description: Integrated software systems unifying finance, HR, operations, and supply chain data.

name: Customer Relationship Management
description: Systems and strategies for managing interactions with current and prospective customers.

name: Business Intelligence
description: Technologies and practices for collecting and analyzing business data to support decisions.

name: Data Warehousing
description: The design of centralized repositories that integrate data for analysis and reporting.

name: Electronic Commerce
description: The conduct of buying, selling, and transacting over electronic networks.

name: Information Systems Strategy
description: The strategic use of information technology to create advantage and enable business strategy.

name: Systems Analysis and Design
description: The structured process of specifying and designing information systems.

name: Business Process Management
description: The systematic analysis, improvement, and automation of business processes.

name: Digital Transformation
description: The organizational reinvention driven by pervasive digital technologies.

name: Corporate Social Responsibility
description: Corporate self-regulation integrating social and environmental concerns into business.

name: Stakeholder Theory
description: The view that firms should create value for all stakeholders, not only shareholders.

name: Sustainability Reporting
description: The disclosure of environmental, social, and governance performance.

name: Business and Human Rights
description: The responsibilities of business to respect and remedy human rights impacts.

name: Ethical Decision Making
description: Frameworks and processes for resolving moral dilemmas in business.

name: Board of Directors
description: The governing body elected by shareholders to oversee management and strategy.

name: Executive Compensation
description: The design and governance of pay and incentives for senior executives.

name: Shareholder Activism
description: Efforts by shareholders to influence corporate policy, governance, or strategy.

name: Audit Committee
description: The board committee overseeing financial reporting, internal controls, and external audit.

name: Agency Theory
description: The analysis of conflicts of interest between principals and their agents, especially owners and managers.

name: Enterprise Risk Management
description: The holistic, organization-wide approach to identifying and managing risk.

name: Corporate Compliance
description: Programs ensuring the firm and its employees follow laws, regulations, and policies.

name: Descriptive Analytics
description: Summarizing historical data to understand what has happened.

name: Predictive Analytics
description: Using statistical models to forecast future outcomes and behavior.

name: Prescriptive Analytics
description: Recommending actions and optimizing decisions using models and simulation.

name: Big Data Analytics
description: Analyzing very large, fast, and varied datasets that exceed traditional tools.

name: Project Planning
description: Defining scope, objectives, deliverables, and approach for a project.

name: Project Scheduling
description: Sequencing tasks and allocating time and resources to complete a project on schedule.

name: Critical Path Method
description: A scheduling technique identifying the longest chain of dependent tasks that determines project duration.

name: Project Cost Management
description: Estimating, budgeting, and controlling project costs.

name: Project Risk Management
description: Identifying, analyzing, and responding to uncertainties in a project.

name: Agile Project Management
description: Iterative, adaptive project delivery emphasizing collaboration and responding to change.

name: Program Management
description: Coordinating a group of related projects to achieve shared benefits.

name: Portfolio Management
description: Selecting and prioritizing the set of projects and programs aligned with strategy.

name: Project Stakeholder Management
description: Identifying and engaging the people and groups who affect or are affected by a project.

name: Open Innovation
description: Innovating by using external ideas and paths to market alongside internal ones.

name: Disruptive Innovation
description: Innovation that displaces incumbents by serving overlooked segments with simpler, cheaper offerings.

name: Design Thinking
description: A human-centered methodology for problem solving that emphasizes empathy, ideation, and prototyping.

name: Technology Management
description: Managing the development, acquisition, and exploitation of technological capabilities.

name: Research and Development Management
description: Managing the research and development function that generates new knowledge and products.

name: Intellectual Property Management
description: Strategically managing patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets.

name: Diffusion of Innovations
description: The study of how, why, and at what rate innovations spread through populations.

name: New Product Development
description: The end-to-end process of bringing a new product from idea to market.

name: Organizational Design
description: The arrangement of structure, roles, and coordination mechanisms in an organization.

name: Organizational Ecology
description: The study of how populations of organizations emerge, compete, and die.

name: Institutional Theory
description: The study of how institutions and legitimacy pressures shape organizational structure and behavior.

name: Resource Dependence Theory
description: The theory that organizations act to secure critical resources and reduce dependence on others.

name: Organizational Learning
description: The processes by which organizations create, retain, and transfer knowledge and adapt.

name: Corporate Finance
description: The financing and investment decisions of corporations to maximize shareholder value.

name: Investments
description: The theory and practice of allocating capital to securities and assets to earn returns.

name: Capital Markets
description: The markets and institutions through which long-term capital is raised and traded.

name: Derivatives
description: Financial instruments whose value derives from an underlying asset, rate, or index.

name: Risk Management
description: The identification, measurement, and mitigation of financial risks.

name: Quantitative Finance
description: The application of mathematics, statistics, and computing to model and price financial instruments.

name: Behavioral Finance
description: The study of how psychological influences affect financial markets and decisions.

name: Public Finance
description: The study of government revenue, expenditure, and debt.

name: Banking
description: The study of financial intermediation and the institutions that take deposits and make loans.

name: Insurance
description: The study of risk transfer through pooled premiums and the institutions that provide it.

name: International Finance
description: The study of financial flows, exchange rates, and markets across national borders.

name: Personal Finance
description: The financial planning and management of household income, assets, and liabilities.

name: Financial Regulation
description: The rules, agencies, and supervision that govern financial markets and institutions.

name: Financial Economics
description: The branch of economics studying the allocation of resources under risk and over time.

name: Financial Technology
description: The use of technology to innovate, automate, and transform financial services.

name: Capital Budgeting
description: Evaluating and selecting long-term investment projects using techniques like NPV and IRR.

name: Cost of Capital
description: The required return on a firm's capital, estimated via models such as CAPM and WACC.

name: Capital Structure
description: The mix of debt and equity a firm uses to finance its operations.

name: Dividend Policy
description: Decisions about whether and how much of earnings to distribute to shareholders.

name: Working Capital Management
description: Managing short-term assets and liabilities, including cash, receivables, and inventory.

name: Valuation
description: Estimating the economic worth of companies, securities, and projects.

name: Discounted Cash Flow Valuation
description: Valuing assets by discounting expected future cash flows to present value.

name: Relative Valuation
description: Valuing assets by comparing them to similar assets using multiples like P/E and EV/EBITDA.

name: Real Options Valuation
description: Valuing managerial flexibility in investments using option-pricing methods.

name: Financial Planning and Analysis
description: The budgeting, forecasting, and analysis that support corporate financial decisions.

name: Corporate Restructuring
description: Reorganizing a firm's capital, assets, or ownership, including mergers, divestitures, and bankruptcy.

name: Portfolio Theory

name: Asset Allocation
description: Distributing a portfolio across asset classes to balance risk and return.

name: Equity Investing
description: Investing in common and preferred stocks and analyzing their value.

name: Fixed Income Investing
description: Investing in bonds and other debt instruments and analyzing their yields and risks.

name: Security Analysis
description: Evaluating individual securities to estimate their intrinsic value.

name: Fundamental Analysis
description: Valuing securities by analyzing financial statements, economics, and competitive position.

name: Technical Analysis
description: Forecasting price movements by studying market statistics, charts, and patterns.

name: Portfolio Management
description: Constructing and overseeing investment portfolios to meet objectives.

name: Active Management
description: Portfolio management that seeks to outperform benchmarks through security selection and timing.

name: Passive Investing
description: Tracking a market index with minimal turnover and low cost.

name: Alternative Investments
description: Investments outside traditional stocks and bonds, including private and illiquid assets.

name: Private Equity
description: Equity investment in unlisted companies through buyouts and growth capital.

name: Venture Capital
description: Equity investment in early-stage, high-growth companies.

name: Hedge Funds
description: Lightly regulated pooled funds using diverse and leveraged strategies across markets.

name: Real Estate Investment
description: Investing in property directly or through vehicles such as REITs.

name: Sustainable Investing
description: Incorporating environmental, social, and governance criteria into investment decisions.

name: Equity Markets
description: Markets for issuing and trading ownership claims in companies.

name: Bond Markets
description: Markets for issuing and trading debt securities of governments and corporations.

name: Money Markets
description: Markets for short-term, highly liquid debt instruments under one year.

name: Foreign Exchange Markets
description: The decentralized global market for trading currencies.

name: Commodity Markets
description: Markets for trading raw materials, energy, metals, and agricultural products.

name: Market Microstructure
description: The study of how trading mechanisms, order flow, and liquidity affect price formation.

name: Primary Markets
description: The market for newly issued securities, including IPOs and underwriting.

name: Secondary Markets
description: The market for trading existing securities among investors.

name: Market Efficiency
description: The degree to which prices reflect all available information, as in the efficient market hypothesis.

name: Options
description: Contracts giving the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a set price.

name: Futures
description: Standardized contracts obligating the exchange of an asset at a future date and price.

name: Swaps
description: Contracts to exchange cash flows, such as interest or currency payments, over time.

name: Forwards
description: Customized contracts to buy or sell an asset at a future date and agreed price.

name: Credit Derivatives
description: Instruments that transfer credit risk, such as credit default swaps.

name: Market Risk
description: The risk of losses from movements in market prices, rates, and volatilities.

name: Credit Risk
description: The risk of loss from a counterparty's failure to meet obligations.

name: Operational Risk
description: The risk of loss from failed internal processes, people, systems, or external events.

name: Liquidity Risk
description: The risk that an asset cannot be traded or obligations met without significant loss.

name: Model Risk
description: The risk of loss from errors or misuse of financial models.

name: Value at Risk
description: A statistical measure of the maximum expected loss over a horizon at a confidence level.

name: Stress Testing
description: Assessing how portfolios and institutions perform under severe but plausible scenarios.

name: Credit Scoring
description: Quantifying borrower creditworthiness using statistical models.

name: Financial Mathematics
description: The mathematical modeling of financial markets and instruments.

name: Option Pricing Models
description: Mathematical models for pricing derivatives, including Black-Scholes and binomial trees.

name: Stochastic Processes in Finance
description: The use of random processes such as Brownian motion to model asset prices.

name: Monte Carlo Simulation
description: A numerical method using random sampling to price derivatives and estimate risk.

name: Algorithmic Trading
description: Executing orders using computer algorithms based on rules and signals.

name: High-Frequency Trading
description: Algorithmic trading at very high speed and volume over extremely short horizons.

name: Machine Learning in Finance
description: Applying machine learning to prediction, pricing, and trading in finance.

name: Risk Modeling
description: Building quantitative models to measure and manage financial risk.

name: Cognitive Biases
description: Systematic mental shortcuts and errors that distort financial judgment.

name: Prospect Theory
description: The theory that people value gains and losses relative to a reference point and are loss-averse.

name: Market Anomalies
description: Empirical price patterns inconsistent with market efficiency, such as momentum and calendar effects.

name: Herding and Bubbles
description: The study of collective imitation and asset price bubbles driven by social influence.

name: Behavioral Corporate Finance
description: How manager and investor biases affect corporate financing and investment decisions.

name: Taxation
description: The study of taxes, their incidence, and their economic effects.

name: Government Budgeting
description: The process of planning, enacting, and executing government revenues and expenditures.

name: Public Debt Management
description: Managing government borrowing and debt obligations sustainably.

name: Fiscal Policy
description: The use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.

name: Public Expenditure
description: The study of government spending, its composition, and its efficiency.

name: Municipal Finance
description: The financing of local government services and infrastructure.

name: Fiscal Federalism
description: The division of taxing and spending responsibilities across levels of government.

name: Commercial Banking
description: The deposit-taking and lending business serving businesses and individuals.

name: Investment Banking
description: Advisory and underwriting services for securities issuance, mergers, and capital raising.

name: Retail Banking
description: Banking services offered directly to individual consumers.

name: Central Banking
description: The study of monetary authority, money supply, and lender-of-last-resort functions.

name: Islamic Banking

name: Shadow Banking

name: Life Insurance

name: Property and Casualty Insurance
description: Insurance covering damage to property and liability for injuries or losses.

name: Reinsurance
description: Insurance purchased by insurers to transfer portions of their risk portfolios.

name: Actuarial Science
description: The application of mathematics and statistics to assess risk in insurance and pensions.

name: Takaful
description: Sharia-compliant cooperative insurance based on mutual contribution.

name: Exchange Rates
description: The determination and behavior of currency prices and exchange rate regimes.

name: International Capital Flows
description: The movement of capital across borders through investment and lending.

name: Sovereign Debt
description: Borrowing by national governments and the risk of default.

name: International Monetary System
description: The institutions and arrangements governing exchange rates and international payments.

name: Financial Planning
description: The comprehensive process of setting and achieving personal financial goals.

name: Retirement Planning
description: Saving and investing to provide income after leaving the workforce.

name: Estate Planning
description: Arranging the transfer of wealth at death and managing associated taxes and documents.

name: Tax Planning
description: Arranging finances to legally minimize tax liabilities.

name: Bank Regulation
description: The supervision of banks' safety, soundness, and conduct.

name: Securities Regulation
description: Rules governing securities issuance, trading, disclosure, and market integrity.

name: Insurance Regulation
description: The oversight of insurers' solvency and consumer protection.

name: Prudential Regulation
description: Capital, liquidity, and risk standards such as the Basel accords.

name: Anti-Money Laundering
description: Laws and controls to detect and prevent the laundering of illicit funds.

name: Asset Pricing
description: The economic theory of how assets are priced, including factor and equilibrium models.

name: Information Asymmetry

name: Contract Theory
description: The design of contracts and incentives under asymmetric information.

name: Agency Theory
description: The analysis of conflicts of interest between principals and agents.

name: Digital Payments
description: Electronic systems for transferring money, including mobile and real-time payments.

name: Peer-to-Peer Lending
description: Direct lending between individuals through online platforms without traditional banks.

name: Robo-Advising
description: Automated, algorithm-driven portfolio management and financial advice.

name: Cryptocurrency

name: Regulatory Technology
description: Technology that automates and improves regulatory compliance.

name: Insurance Technology
description: Technology-driven innovation in insurance distribution, underwriting, and claims.

name: Financial Accounting

name: Financial Reporting
description: Preparing financial statements in accordance with accounting standards.

name: Revenue Recognition
description: Determining when and how much revenue should be recognized in the accounts.

name: Asset Accounting

name: Liability and Equity Accounting

name: Consolidated Financial Statements

name: Financial Statement Analysis
description: Evaluating a company's performance and position using ratios and other analytical tools.

name: Earnings Management

name: International Financial Reporting Standards
description: The global accounting standards issued by the IASB.

name: Managerial Accounting
description: Accounting information for internal planning, control, and decision making.

name: Cost Accounting
description: Measuring and analyzing the costs of products, services, and activities.

name: Process Costing
